items.requirement: Define the exact production responsibility of Local service chaining.
Document what Local service chaining owns and explicitly does not own.
Identify upstream, downstream, and peer dependencies of Local service chaining.
Define the authoritative source of truth used by Local service chaining.
Document assumptions Local service chaining makes about nodes, runtimes, networks, storage, and control planes.
Define tenant, environment, site, and workload boundaries relevant to Local service chaining.
Separate mandatory Local service chaining capabilities from optional optimizations.
Document unsupported deployment patterns and non-goals for Local service chaining.
Assign an accountable owner and escalation path for Local service chaining.
Approve an architecture decision record for Local service chaining, its technologies (Direct component handler composition), and its function (Eliminate unnecessary local HTTP/gRPC hops).
Translate the source function of Local service chaining — Eliminate unnecessary local HTTP/gRPC hops — into testable SHALL-level requirements.
Define functional requirements for Local service chaining across cloud, datacenter, near-edge, and far-edge contexts where applicable.
Define non-functional requirements for latency, availability, durability, consistency, isolation, or determinism as applicable.
Define success, partial success, degraded operation, retryable failure, and terminal failure semantics for Local service chaining.
Define lifecycle states and legal state transitions managed or exposed by Local service chaining.
Define versioning and backward-compatibility requirements for Local service chaining.
Define capacity ceilings, quotas, and fairness semantics relevant to Local service chaining.
Define behavior when network connectivity is intermittent or absent.
Define precedence rules when Local service chaining requirements conflict with security, residency, SLO, or cost constraints.
Maintain a requirements traceability matrix from each Local service chaining requirement to implementation and verification evidence.
Enumerate every API, WIT contract, RPC, event, file, device, hypervisor, or control-plane boundary exposed by Local service chaining.
Use versioned typed schemas for all externally visible Local service chaining contracts.
Define authentication requirements at each Local service chaining boundary.
Define authorization and explicit capability requirements at each Local service chaining boundary.
Define timeout, cancellation, retry, idempotency, and backpressure semantics for Local service chaining.
Define structured failure codes and machine-readable error details for Local service chaining.
Define compatibility behavior when peers use different supported versions.
Document payload, concurrency, queue, connection, or resource limits at Local service chaining interfaces.
Provide reference examples and conformance fixtures for Local service chaining.
Create automated integration tests proving Local service chaining interoperates with adjacent architectural layers.
Select and pin approved implementations, versions, or specifications for Local service chaining: Direct component handler composition.
Separate immutable artifacts from mutable configuration and state for Local service chaining.
Define declarative configuration and secure defaults for Local service chaining.
Validate configuration before activation and fail closed on security-critical errors.
Support site- and environment-specific configuration without rebuilding immutable artifacts.
Record configuration provenance, version, author, and activation time.
Apply atomic or transactional configuration updates where partial application is unsafe.
Define automatic and operator-driven rollback for failed Local service chaining changes.
Keep credentials and secret material out of ordinary Local service chaining configuration and diagnostics.
Provide a deterministic bootstrap path from an empty node/environment to healthy Local service chaining operation.
Threat-model Local service chaining against malicious tenants, compromised workloads, hostile inputs, supply-chain compromise, and control-plane abuse.
Apply least privilege to every identity and capability used by Local service chaining.
Eliminate ambient filesystem, network, device, kernel, and secret authority wherever Local service chaining permits.
Authenticate nodes, peers, artifacts, providers, and control-plane actors before trust is granted.
Verify signatures, digests, provenance, and approved versions for executable or policy artifacts consumed by Local service chaining.
Enforce tenant/workload isolation across Local service chaining execution, memory, state, network, and device boundaries as applicable.
Encrypt sensitive Local service chaining data in transit and at rest with managed key rotation.
items.residual: TLS supported/enforced off-loopback; at-rest encryption of audit log is an estate storage control

items.requirement: Define safe behavior when identity, attestation, policy, key, or time services are unavailable.
Emit tamper-evident audit events for security-sensitive Local service chaining operations.
Run adversarial tests for privilege escalation, injection, replay, spoofing, escape, side channels, and resource exhaustion.
Enumerate component, process, VM, node, site, network, provider, dependency, and control-plane failures affecting Local service chaining.
Define automated health and stall detection thresholds for Local service chaining.
Implement bounded retry with backoff and jitter only where operations are safe to retry.
Implement admission control, load shedding, or circuit breaking to prevent Local service chaining failure cascades.
Define failover behavior without violating isolation, residency, or consistency requirements.
Provide degraded operation when noncritical dependencies are unavailable.
Define crash-consistency, restart, resume, or replay semantics for mutable Local service chaining state.
Protect against split-brain, duplicate ownership, stale controllers, or duplicate execution where relevant.
Provide quarantine, freeze, disable, or isolation controls for unsafe Local service chaining behavior.
Run fault-injection tests proving Local service chaining recovery against documented objectives.
Establish reproducible baselines for Local service chaining latency, throughput, startup, CPU, memory, storage, network, and power overhead.
Define p50, p95, p99, and worst-case performance thresholds for Local service chaining.
Measure Local service chaining under steady load, burst load, overload, scale-out, scale-in, and recovery.
Measure per-workload and per-tenant overhead introduced by Local service chaining.
Identify avoidable serialization, copies, context switches, network hops, duplicated images, or duplicated state in Local service chaining.
Apply locality, caching, direct composition, batching, zero-copy, or kernel-bypass optimizations where semantics permit.
Bound memory growth, queue depth, buffer size, concurrency, and resource fan-out.
Measure power and thermal impact on constrained edge nodes where relevant.
Define capacity models and saturation signals that predict when Local service chaining needs more resources.
Block releases that regress approved Local service chaining startup, density, throughput, or tail-latency thresholds.
Expose Local service chaining health, readiness, version, configuration, dependency status, and active capability set.
Emit structured metrics for rate, errors, latency, saturation, backlog, and resource use.
Emit structured logs with stable node, tenant, workload, component, and operation identifiers.
Propagate trace context across all relevant Local service chaining boundaries.
Expose high-cardinality diagnostic detail safely without leaking tenant or secret data.
Record the reason for every automated decision made by Local service chaining.
Provide an operator-readable explain view linking decisions to input state, policies, topology, and constraints.
Correlate Local service chaining events with application release lineage and the live infrastructure graph.
Define telemetry retention, sampling, privacy, and export policy.
Create dashboards and alerts distinguishing ordinary load, degradation, policy rejection, dependency failure, attack, and software defect.
Create unit tests for deterministic Local service chaining logic and state transitions.
Create contract tests for every public Local service chaining interface.
Create integration tests with every supported adjacent layer and execution tier.
Create compatibility tests across supported CPU architectures, runtimes, hypervisors, providers, and protocol versions relevant to Local service chaining.
Fuzz parsers, schemas, protocol handlers, WIT/RPC boundaries, or untrusted inputs handled by Local service chaining.
Create concurrency and race-condition tests for shared/distributed Local service chaining state.
Create security tests derived directly from the Local service chaining threat model.
Create benchmark, soak, burst, and fleet-scale tests appropriate to Local service chaining.
Create disaster, partition, reconnect, and degraded-control-plane tests.
Require machine-readable acceptance evidence before certifying a Local service chaining release for production.
Define production SLOs, error budgets, and support commitments for Local service chaining.
Define canary, staged rollout, rollback, and emergency-disable procedures for Local service chaining.
Maintain a supported-version compatibility matrix for Local service chaining and adjacent dependencies.
Define patching, vulnerability response, and end-of-life SLAs for Local service chaining.
Provide backup, restore, migration, or reconstruction procedures for Local service chaining state where applicable.
Create day-0 bootstrap, day-1 deployment, and day-2 operation runbooks.
Define incident severity, paging, escalation, containment, and recovery procedures.
Perform recurring access, policy, dependency, configuration, and architecture reviews.
Track exceptions, waivers, technical debt, and deprecated behaviors with owners and expiry dates.
Require a formal production exit gate confirming architecture, requirements, interfaces, implementation, security, resilience, performance, observability, testing, rollback, and ownership readiness.
